title: A finite intermediate integral ring has a conductor power
statement: Let B be a Noetherian semilocal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with Jacobson radical m_B, let K be its fraction field, and let A be a finite B-algebra contained in K. If A and B have the same fraction field, then there exists an integer n>0 such that m_B^n A is contained in B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Submodule.FG.of_finite to A.toSubmodule and FractionalIdeal.isFractional_of_fg (Mathlib/RingTheory/FractionalIdeal/Operations.lean:171) to obtain a common denominator d in the non-zero-divisors of B such that d times every element of A is in the image of B. Since B is a domain, d is nonzero. This replaces the finite-quotient generic-support calculation by clearing the denominators of a finite generating set.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: For any prime ideal P containing (d), d is in P and d is nonzero, so P is nonzero. The dimension bound from ringKrullDim B = 1 gives Ring.KrullDimLE 1 B; Mathlib Ideal.IsPrime.isMaximal_of_ne_bot makes P maximal. Hence the intersection of all maximal ideals, jacobson(0), is contained in each prime over (d). Ideal.radical_eq_sInf, the intersection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], gives jacobson(0) contained in radical((d)). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] to the Noetherian (and therefore finitely generated) ideal jacobson(0). If n is the resulting exponent, take n+1; ideal powers decrease as the exponent increases.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: For b in jacobson(0)^(n+1), its membership in (d) gives b=r*d. For any a in A, the common-denominator property gives c in B with image(c)=image(d)*a. Multiplicativity and associativity show image(r*c)=image(b)*a.
